items.title: Social media pictures of wife enjoying life can't prove ability to maintain herself: Gauhati High Court
items.summary: The Gauhati High Court recently held that a wife's social media posts showing her enjoying life cannot, by themselves, establish that she is financially independent or capable of maintaining herself. A Division Bench of Justices Michael Zothankhuma and Sanjeev Kumar Sharma made the observation while setting aside a family court order that had denied a woman maintenance from her husband. The family court had denied maintenance after noting that the woman had uploaded social media posts showing her "enjoyful life at Guwahati". It had questioned how she was financing her lifestyle and observed that she was an able-bodied woman who could find employment to support herself. Disagreeing with this reasoning, the High Court said, "The finding of the learned Family Court that the petitioner-wife is having an 'enjoyable life at Guwahati' as uploaded by her on social media does not, in our view, prove that the petitioner-wife was able to finance her lifestyle through employment." The case arose from a marriage solemnised in March 2023. The couple separated approximately three months later. The wife had approached the family court seeking maintenance of ₹15,000 per month. items.title: Ariyil Shukkoor murder: 13 found guilty; CPI(M) leaders Jayarajan, Rajesh acquitted
items.summary: Eighteen accused, including senior leaders of Communist Party of India (Marxist) P Jayarajan and TV Rajesh, were acquitted in the murder case of Ariyil Shukkoor, a member of the Muslim Students Federation (MSF). A special CBI court in Kochi on Thursday, November 19, found 13 persons guilty in the case. The quantum of the sentence will be pronounced at 3 PM. Shukkoor, 24, was murdered on February 20, 2012 by a vigilante mob, following an attack on the vehicle used by Jayarajan and Rajesh to visit Pattuvam in Kannur during a League-CPI(M) conflict. Jayarajan, then Kannur district secretary of CPI(M) and Rajesh, then an MLA, were accused of conspiracy in the murder. According to reports, Shukkoor was subjected to a ‘Kangaroo court’ trial for around two hours by the CPI(M) workers before he was stabbed to death. Special judge CBI-III (Ernakulam) P Sabarinathan found accused Sumesh KV, Anoop, Pavithran P, Manoharan PV, NP Ajith Kumar, P P Suresan, EP Radhakrishnan, Shijin Mohan @ Shijin, KV Sajith, VV Mohanan, Purushothaman MV @ Purushu, P K Ajith Kumar, and P P Suresan as guilty. As the world eased into the new year in January 2022, a committee at Deutsche Bank headquarters in Frankfurt prepared to discuss if the bank should go ahead with deals which could hurt its reputation. items.title: Supreme Court quashes Odisha's 2021 land acquisition for Dalmia Cement mining project
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside the State of Odisha’s acquisition of land in three villages in Sundargarh district for a Dalmia Cement mining project. [Bibol Toppo v. Odisha] A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma held that the State proceeded without obtaining the mandatory consent of the gram sabhas and affected families. It overturned the Orissa High Court’s September 2024 judgment upholding the acquisition. It further said that the High Court’s treatment of gram sabha consent had “the effect of reducing a mandatory statutory requirement into a paper formality.” “ Far from a meaningful consent, there is not even paper consent of Gram Sabha in this case, ” the Court said, noting that both gram sabhas had rejected the proposal in January 2020. Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Satish Chandra Sharma Dalmia Cement already held a mining lease extending to 2040. In 2015, it asked the Odisha government to acquire surface rights over agricultural land in Kukuda, Bihabandha and Lanjiberna so it could expand mining operations. items.title: Kerala police bring back absconding murder accused from Dubai after 18 years
items.summary: A man who was absconding for nearly 18 years in a murder case in Kerala’s Thrissur was brought back to India from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and arrested with the assistance of Interpol. The accused, Rakesh Unnikochan (46), also identified as Raghesh Unnikochan in the Central Bureau of Investigation’s (CBI) statement, is the third accused in the murder of Dhanesh, a resident of Thirumangalam in Engandiyur, Thrissur. He was apprehended in Dubai following the issuance of an Interpol Red Corner Notice (RCN) and deported to India on Wednesday, November 19. The CBI, which functions as India’s National Central Bureau for Interpol, secured the RCN at the request of the Kerala Police. The UAE authorities subsequently traced and arrested Rakesh. He had reportedly remained in detention in Dubai for four months after the notice was issued. A chargesheet had already been filed in the case and the court had issued an open-ended arrest warrant against him. A police team from Kerala travelled to Dubai to take custody of the accused and bring him back.
